figures.finding: India's national production incentive reimburses 30% of qualifying spend in India (plus 5% for at least 15% Indian crew and 5% for significant Indian content, up to 40%), capped at ₹30 crore a project, for foreign productions through an Indian service company and for official treaty co-productions, where the Indian co-producer claims 30%; live shoots must spend at least ₹3 crore in India, and the scheme's budget was ₹150 crore a year for 2023-24 and 2024-25, paid first come first served.

value.administeredBy: Film Facilitation Office (NFDC), managed by Invest India

figures.applies: India, foreign films and official co-productions under India's bilateral audiovisual treaties; revised guidelines read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Upto 40% of the qualifying production expenditure incurred in India, with an enhanced cap of the incentive payout of Rupees 300 Million/ INR 30 Crore (significant enhancement from earlier limit of Rupees 2.5 Cr), can be claimed by the Indian Production Services Company on behalf of the Foreign Production or the Official Co-production. The scheme is administered by the Film Facilitation Office set up by the Ministry under National Film Development Corporation and managed by Invest India. … Minimum Qualifying Production Expenditure (QPE) of Rs 3 Crore/ INR 30 Million in India (Nil for Documentaries) … Reimbursement of upto 30% of QPE. o Bonus incentive of 5% of QPE for employing at least 15% Indian Labour. o Additional bonus incentive of 5% of QPE for Significant Indian Content. … For the first two years i.e financial years 2023-24 and 2024-25, the total available budget will be Rs 1.5 Billion/150 Crore each. … Reimbursement of 30% of Qualifying Production Expenditure (QPE) incurred in India subject to a cap of INR 300 million/ Rs 30 Crore per project. … Application to be made by Indian Coproducer

figures.finding: India's film board certified 3,164 feature films in 2025 (2,357 for theatrical release, the rest for video or digital, dubbed versions counted separately); by language Hindi had 601 (322 theatrical), Tamil 500, Kannada 411, Telugu 396, Malayalam 351, Bhojpuri 168, Bengali 166 and Marathi 136.

figures.finding: Indian feature films are made in many languages, not one: of the 3,164 certified in 2025, Hindi was the largest single language (601) but Tamil, Kannada, Telugu and Malayalam together had 1,658, and at least 25 languages appear in the list.

figures.finding: India's main producers' body is the Producers Guild of India, founded in 1954 as The Film Producers Guild of India Ltd and covering television since 2004, which represents film, television and digital producers before government on regulation, copyright, tax and incentives.

sources.said: Producers Guild of India (GUILD) is the premier film, television and digital content producers’ body representing the pre-eminent producers of audio-visual content in India … Established as ‘The Film Producers Guild of India Ltd’ in 1954 by stalwarts of the Indian film industry including Raj Kapoor, Mehboob Khan, Sasadhar Mukerji, B.N. Sircar, V. Shantaram, Vijay Bhatt, B.R. Chopra, Guild incorporated the television sector within its fold in 2004
